source.author: stat
source.text: mirabar, cur templa mihi tremuisse Dianae nuper et inferior vultu dea visa, sacrisque exuviae cecidere tholis; hoc segnior arcus difficilesque manus et nullo in vulnere certae.
source.text_original: mirabar, cur templa mihi tremuisse Dianae / nuper et inferior vultu dea visa, sacrisque / exuviae cecidere tholis; hoc segnior arcus / difficilesque manus et nullo in vulnere certae.
source.text_english: I was wondering why the temples of my Diana had lately trembled for me, and why the goddess had seemed to look downward, and the spoils had fallen from the sacred domes: this explains my bow’s slowness, my hands’ ineptitude, and their certainty in dealing no wound.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: tu, cui iam curaeque vigent animique viriles, i, decus, et pecoris Nephelaei vellera Graio redde tholo ac tantis temet dignare periclis.
reuse.text_original: tu, cui iam curaeque vigent animique viriles, / i, decus, et pecoris Nephelaei vellera Graio / redde tholo ac tantis temet dignare periclis.
reuse.text_english: You, in whom now both cares and manly courage are strong, go, my glory, and restore to the Greek shrine the fleece of the Nephelaean flock, and deem yourself worthy of so great dangers.
